item.content:encoded: No revisiting 'Sandpapergate': Cricket Australia CEO refuses to re-open investigation over Usman Khawaja's statement originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Cricket Australia ’s chief executive has made his position clear on Sandpapergate. Usman Khawaja's book revelations have reopened an old and bitter debate. Former teammates are divided, and the board sees little reason to look again. MORE: '100% accurate': David Warner backs Usman Khawaja's Sandpapergate claims, questions Cricket Australia's 2018 investigation CA refuses to budge: Why Cricket Australia won't revisit Sandpapergate despite Usman Khawaja's bombshell Cricket Australia has no plans to go back to ‘Sandpapergate’, and chief executive Todd Greenberg has firmly refused to reopen the investigation despite the startling claims made by Usman Khawaja. The board, he says, is content with how the inquiry into the 2018 ball-tampering affair ended, even though Khawaja now insists that the whole team knew sandpaper was being used on that tour of South Africa. Greenberg's statement arrived just after David Warner threw his weight behind his old teammate, describing the account as “100 per cent accurate” and calling the original investigation “rushed and botched”. MORE: Khawaja sides with Warner, Smith and Bancroft in 'Sandpaper scandal' Khawaja tells his side of the story in his autobiography, Sabr, and it appears to clash with a joint statement released in 2021 by Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon. In that statement, the four bowlers said they had no idea the ball was being tampered with. The left-hander has also spoken of his surprise that Cricket Australia never interviewed him, even though he sat beside Cameron Bancroft throughout the Cape Town Test. Greenberg, however, has made it clear that the book alone will not change the board’s mind. He spoke to SEN about the matter, and his comments touched on his respect for Khawaja, his unwillingness to react to headlines and his belief that nothing useful would come from another inquiry. MORE: ‘We knew': Khawaja blows apart Cummins, Starc's claims of innocence in sandpaper scandal Getty Images Todd Greenberg’s first reaction to Khawaja’s claims about Sandpapergate Greenberg admitted that he had not yet found the time to read the book and said Khawaja had been thoughtful enough to warn him about the release some months earlier. “I haven’t read the book yet. Clearly it is out, but I’ll hopefully get an opportunity to do it, but Usman was good enough to let me know some months ago that he would be releasing a book, and I really appreciated that call,” Greenberg told SEN. He then spoke about the respect he holds for the batter and explained that he had learned about the claims in the same way as everyone else. “First and foremost, I have huge respect for Usman to give his version of events,” he added. “I read his comments over the weekend in the media, exactly the same time as the public and I’ll obviously get to read his book at some point." MORE: 'He is accurate': Former Aussie quick, part of Sandpapergate tour, backs up Khawaja Next came a note of caution. Greenberg pointed out that parts of Khawaja’s account run against what other people have said, and he stressed that he wants to respond only to the batter’s actual words rather than to the noise around them. He added: “But there are specific details in his book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others. And I want to be really careful to consider what Usman’s actually said, and not respond to the headlines or the subsequent commentary that gets created. “It’s important to attribute his words and not the headlines. It’s important to know that back at that time, players were urged to come forward, and they had the opportunity to do so over these past eight years, and that remains the case.” MORE: Khawaja sides with Warner, Smith and Bancroft in 'Sandpaper scandal' Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft bans: Why Cricket Australia stands by its original investigation The inquiry that followed the Cape Town Test led to 12-month suspensions for Steve Smith and Warner, who were captain and vice-captain at the time. Bancroft, the young opener who handled the sandpaper, was banned for nine months. Greenberg said nothing in Khawaja’s account has shifted the board’s thinking about that process in any way. “We have said we’re comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we’ve received. That includes what we’ve seen from Usman, and our position hasn’t changed on that,” he said. He went on to rule out a fresh review in plain terms, adding that he cannot see anyone gaining from it. “We don’t see any compelling reason to open the investigation or revisit this again. I don’t think there’s anything that can be gained from that.” Warner has asked for those who ran the original investigation to be held answerable, but Greenberg wondered aloud what a second look would actually achieve. His main worry is that the argument would simply return to where it already stands, with one person’s memory set against another’s. “You end up at the same intersection where one person’s version of events contradicts the others, and I’m not sure what outcome people are searching for,” he said. “I think what people want is a single outcome that everyone is aligned up on, but I don’t think that’s possible on this occasion because we have such conflicting views from the same moment in time.” MORE: 'They cheated': Fans react to Khawaja's Sandpapergate revelations (Getty Images) Why Cricket Australia’s refusal to reopen the Sandpapergate inquiry will not end the debate Greenberg’s argument has a certain logic, since a fresh inquiry could well end up in the same stalemate of clashing memories. However, that is a weak reason to close the door on a matter where Khawaja, the one who sat beside Bancroft throughout the Cape Town Test, was never even asked for his version. The board is also leaning heavily on the idea that players had eight years to come forward. That sounds fair on paper, yet it ignores the fear that many of them must have felt after watching three colleagues serve lengthy bans. It is hard to expect honesty from people who believe that speaking up could cost them their careers. There is a further problem of trust. Warner, Khawaja and the four bowlers are all telling different stories, and the public can see that. A board that simply declares itself comfortable with the outcome will struggle to convince fans that the original process was thorough, especially when it admits that it did not speak to a man who was closest to Bancroft in Cape Town. Cricket Australia need not rewrite the punishments to restore some confidence. A limited, transparent review of how the first investigation was run, and why certain players were never questioned, would cost very little. By refusing even that, the board risks keeping Sandpapergate alive for years to come. For all the latest cricket news, opinion, and commentary, and to share your voice, head to our Facebook , Instagram, and X (Twitter) pages.

item.title: Week 10 Fantasy Football Injury Report: Puka Nacua, Patrick Mahomes, Josh Jacobs And More
item.description: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams runs the ball against the Washington Commanders during the fourth quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. If your roster isn’t being held together by duct tape right now, you’re in great shape. The 2026 NFL season has been brutal from an injury standpoint, and Week 9 brought another onslaught of notable ailments. A handful of starting quarterbacks suffered injuries that could jeopardize their availability for Week 10 and beyond. A pair of starting running backs went down with injuries that will sideline them for at least one week. And a number of fantasy-relevant wide receivers are also on the mend after suffering injuries on Sunday. Mahomes underwent an MRI after the game, and sources told NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport that the tests “did not reveal a major injury.” Rapoport added that “Mahomes’ elbow strain/sprain will be monitored over the next few days for pain and swell. But so far, so good.” For now, it seems as though Mahomes should be able to suit up in Week 10 against the Atlanta Falcons. But pay close attention to the Chiefs’ injury reports at practice, as it wouldn’t be surprising if Mahomes is limited, especially early in the week. item.content:encoded: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams runs the ball against the Washington Commanders during the fourth quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 08, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Getty Images We’re about one month out from the start of the fantasy football playoffs. If your roster isn’t being held together by duct tape right now, you’re in great shape. The 2026 NFL season has been brutal from an injury standpoint, and Week 9 brought another onslaught of notable ailments. A handful of starting quarterbacks suffered injuries that could jeopardize their availability for Week 10 and beyond. A pair of starting running backs went down with injuries that will sideline them for at least one week. And a number of fantasy-relevant wide receivers are also on the mend after suffering injuries on Sunday. Every week, we’ll be breaking down the biggest injury news that could shape your fantasy football lineup moving forward. Let’s dive into all of the most notable updates ahead of Week 10. Notable QB Injuries Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes (elbow) The Kansas City Chiefs’ season nearly went off the rails Sunday. Late in the second quarter of their eventual blowout win over the New York Jets, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes left the field holding his elbow after getting hit by Jets edge-rusher David Bailey as he was attempting a throw. Luckily, he was able to return to the game on the Chiefs’ next offensive possession. Mahomes underwent an MRI after the game, and sources told NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport that the tests “did not reveal a major injury.” Rapoport added that “Mahomes’ elbow strain/sprain will be monitored over the next few days for pain and swell. But so far, so good.” For now, it seems as though Mahomes should be able to suit up in Week 10 against the Atlanta Falcons. But pay close attention to the Chiefs’ injury reports at practice, as it wouldn’t be surprising if Mahomes is limited, especially early in the week. Chargers QB Justin Herbert (hand) Just when you thought the Los Angeles Chargers’ season couldn’t be going any worse, quarterback Justin Herbert left midway through the fourth quarter of his team’s blowout loss to the Houston Texans with an injury to the middle finger on his left (non-throwing) hand. According to ESPN , Herbert “said he wanted to stay in the game, but coach Jim Harbaugh said he overruled him.” However, Harbaugh told reporters Monday that X-rays on Herbert’s hand came back negative for a fracture, “so he should be good to go.” Even with Herbert active, there might not be a single Chargers skill-position player who should be in fantasy lineups in 10- or 12-team leagues. They’ve been that much of a mess this season. Giants QB J.J. McCarthy (hip) New York Giants quarterback left his team’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles in the third quarter with a hip injury after taking a big hit from Eagles linebacker Zack Baun. He missed the Giants’ ensuing drive—and backup Jameis Winston went 6-of-8 for 71 yards and a touchdown on said drive—before returning to finish out the game, albeit hobbled. After the game, McCarthy told reporters that he felt “good” and that “we’re going to do our best to make sure we turn over as fast as possible and do whatever we can between now and then and make sure we’re as close to 100% leading up to a great opponent against Washington.” Unfortunately for McCarthy, the Giants are facing the Commanders on Thursday Night Football in Week 10, so he’s facing a tighter-than-usual turnaround. On Monday, Giants head coach John Harbaugh told reporters that McCarthy is “doing well” and it “does look like he’s going to play” against Washington. But regardless of whether McCarthy or Winston starts under center, Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely should be in all fantasy lineups. Seahawks QB Drew Lock (oblique) Seattle Seahawks starting quarterback Sam Darnold missed his team’s Week 9 win over the Arizona Cardinals with a quad injury and a cracked rib, and he’s not expected to return their Week 10 game against the Las Vegas Raiders, either. But he isn’t the only Seahawks quarterback who’s nursing multiple injuries. Drew Lock, who started in Darnold’s place on Sunday, came into the game with an elbow injury and suffered an oblique injury during the game as well. But during a radio appearance Monday, MacDonald said the Seahawks got a “good exam for Drew” and “I think it’s something we can manage,” according to Seahawks reporter John Boyle . Lock’s availability for Week 10 is great news for fantasy managers who’ve been relying on star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The Seahawks otherwise would have been down to third-string quarterback Jalen Milroe, who has attempted only three regular-season passes thus far in his NFL career. Cardinals QB Gardner Minshew (elbow) On Friday, the Arizona Cardinals officially traded quarterback Jacoby Brissett, whom they benched for Gardner Minshew in Week 8, to the Baltimore Ravens. Three days later, they might be having some seller’s remorse. According to Rapoport , Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm” against the Seahawks. He suffered the injury before halftime and played through it in the second half, but Rapoport added that he now might be out for the rest of the season. If that’s the case, rookie quarterback Carson Beck will now be in line to start, albeit with a depleted pass-catching corps. (More on that later.) Beck will have little choice but to pepper tight end Trey McBride with targets moving forward, although McBride’s chances of racking up touchdowns might go down exponentially if Minshew is done for the year. Notable RB Injuries Packers RB Josh Jacobs (finger) Josh Jacobs’ return to the Green Bay Packers lineup didn’t last long. In only his third game back after a six-game suspension, Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the first quarter of his team’s blowout win over the New England Patriots and did not return. After the game, head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that “hopefully we can do something to allow him to go out there, but he was just having a hard time gripping the ball.” However, CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reported Monday that Jacobs is “set to undergo surgery on his injured finger this week and is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks.” With Jacobs sidelined, Kaleb Johnson led the way in Green Bay’s backfield with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown, while Pierre Strong Jr. added eight carries for 22 yards. If Marshawn Lloyd returns this week—he missed Sunday’s game with a knee injury—the Packers could be right back to a three-headed backfield that is a fantasy football quagmire. Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) With fellow New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson dealing with an “ unexpected and unusual medical emergency ,” Rhamondre Stevenson dominated the Patriots’ backfield in Week 8 with a season-high 19 carries for 82 yards. He was on pace for another hefty workload against the Packers—he had six carries for 32 yards and three catches for 46 yards—until he suffered a knee injury in the third quarter and did not return. On Monday, Schefter reported that Stevenson “is dealing with a knee tendon issue that is not expected to require surgery but could sideline him for a short period of time.” Rapoport added that “the injury is to the back of Stevenson’s knee and is expected to keep him out the next few weeks.” Corey Kiner led the Patriots with eight carries for 55 yards and a touchdown against the Packers, so he figures to get the first crack at the starting job with Stevenson and Henderson sidelined. The Pats could always pursue an upgrade on the trade market ahead of the NFL trade deadline at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, too. Notable WR/TE Injuries Rams WR Puka Nacua (knee) With Davante Adams sidelined for the past few weeks, Puka Nacua has become the clear focal point of the Los Angeles

Jacksonville is running away with the AFC South, so it's just now a matter of whether it can lock down the No. 1 seed. 7. Minnesota Vikings 5-2 (5) The Vikings went into Monday night's loss to the Bills averaging only 20 points per game, scoring at a pace with some of the league's worst teams. Pittsburgh Steelers 6-2 (8) The Steelers are more confident they can win big in Aaron Rodgers' presumed final season. Seattle Seahawks 5-4 (9) The Seahawks got back to their ideal 50-50 offense to dominate the Cardinals, with 28 Drew Lock passes to match the number of non-Lock runs. He's starting to press and force the issue in the passing game as the defense keeps struggling, not a good formula. 15. They are winning several battles of attrition, just outlasting opponents, but they should not apologize for how much mental toughness John Harbaugh has instilled in them. So much for knocking him for the Ravens' blown leads. 16. Cleveland Browns 5-4 (16) The Browns' aggressive nature with first-year coach Todd Monken should be applauded. Even though they didn't win the overtime game in New Orleans, seeing their passing game click so much with Shedeur Sanders is inspiring. Making the playoffs is less important than finding out whether Sanders can be their franchise QB. MORE: Five reasons why Browns should keep starting Sanders at QB 17. They outlasted the Colts with near-perfect balance, with 37 Prescott dropbacks matched by 34 total runs. That's the formula the Cowboys need: A lot more Javonte Williams. MORE: Ranking 7 trade deadline landing spots for Jonathan Taylor 18. Houston Texans 3-5 (26) C.J. Stroud lit up the Chargers for 384 yards and 5 TDs, bringing him up to an average of 281 yards per game and on pace for 34 TDs. He's averaging 8.0 yards per attempt with a 112.1 passer rating. He's all but locked up his lucrative second contract. 19. Las Vegas Raiders 4-5 (18) The Raiders went to San Francisco, allowing an average of 146.4 rushing yards per game, the second-highest total in the NFL. item.title: The Bills are in first place in the AFC following their Monday night win
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Terrel Bernard #8 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates with teammates after intercepting a pass intended for Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings during the third quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills beat the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night to hold onto their spot atop the AFC. It wasn’t easy, but the Bills put enough points on the board to get it done. In the AFC East, the New England Patriots also lost as did the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins. The Bills are up two games in the win column and three games in the loss column. A dominating lead in the division right now with plenty of games left. The AFC divisional leaders aw the Jacksonville Jaguars win on Thursday nigh tand the Denver Broncos win on Sunday with the Pittsburgh Steelers on a bye. The seven AFC playoff teams seem pretty darn set. AFC playoff standings after Bills’ MNF win 1. Buffalo Bills (7-1) 2. Denver Broncos (7-2) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2, 5-2 AFC) 4. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2, win over CIN, 3-2 AFC) 5. Kansas City Chiefs (6-2, 6-1 AFC) 6. Cincinnati Bengals (6-2, loss to PIT, 4-2 AFC) 7. New England Patriots (5-4, 5-1 AFC) 8. Cleveland Browns (5-4, 3-3 AFC) 9. Las Vegas Raiders (4-5, 3-3 AFC) 10. Baltimore Ravens (4-5, 2-4 AFC) 11. Houston Texans (3-5) 12. New York Jets (2-7, 2-4 AFC) 13. Indianapolis Colts (2-7, 1-5 AFC) 14. Miami Dolphins (1-7, 1-4 AFC) 15. Tennessee Titans (1-7, 1-5 AFC) 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) Explaining the 6-2 logjam in the AFC playoff standings The Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals are both 6-2, so they first have to settle the AFC North leader. Pittsburgh’s win over the Bengals slots the Steelers into the division lead. Among the division leaders, the Jaguars and Steelers haven’t played each other so the Jags’ 5-2 AFC record slots them third in front of the Steelers. In the Wild card, the Chiefs and Bengals are tied. The Chiefs have the best AFC record at 6-1, so they fill in at fifth. The Bengals are sixth.

item.title: Oregon braces for a 'different' Michigan after OC firing, QB shake-up
item.description: The Oregon football team and coach Dan Lanning are set to take on a reeling Michigan program with a fired offensive coordinator and major questions at quarterback. Sound familiar? The Ducks (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten) went through their own offensive crisis in mid-October, fired offensive play-caller Drew Mehringer and shuffled quarterbacks before finally hitting their groove in each of the last two weeks. Lanning is expecting the Wolverines (5-4, 2-4) to look like a different team this Saturday, Nov. 14, at Autzen Stadium. "Teams that have done that and experienced that recently, they’ve kind of had a resurgence on offense," Lanning said during his Nov. 9 press conference. And Lanning isn't just talking about his Ducks . The fifth-year coach has shown his players clips, stats and other information around programs that have made major coaching changes midseason and performed significantly better in the ensuing weeks. "We’ve seen a lot of those teams have a lot of success," Lanning said. "And sometimes that’s not just because of a change, but there’s a spark that’s sometimes lit when those things happen. We anticipate to see their absolute best and we’re going to have to chase ghosts a little bit and look for every answer that we might be able to find based on what might be different." Michigan has been putrid offensively over the last month-plus, ranking nearly dead-last in college football in total offense (302.6 yards per game) and scoring offense (19.6 points per game). The Wolverines are fresh off a miserable offensive showing in a rivalry loss to Michigan State last weekend at home, scoring a meager six points and turning the ball over four times. Bryce Underwood, a former consensus five-star recruit, was benched at quarterback for freshman Tommy Carr, but neither signal caller has had much success this season. Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham, who is in his first season in Ann Arbor after 22 seasons as the head coach of Utah, said he'd re-evaluate the QB situation this weekend. He also fired his OC, Jason Beck. Underwood has completed 58.1% of his passes for 924 yards, five touchdowns and six interceptions while Carr has completed 67% of his throws for 641 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. "More recently, I think if you look at it, it’s about who’s been protecting the ball better," Lanning said of the Michigan QBs. "Bryce, obviously, the strength of his arm and as a running threat is unique. But they both operate some similar – it isn’t like the offense completely changes based on which guy’s in the game. There’s still some similarities in what they do." Lanning said the Ducks will look back at film of Michigan's newest play-caller, offensive line coach Jim Harding, and do a deep dive of what Whittingham's offenses have looked like over the years in Salt Lake City. After four seasons at UC Santa Barbara, Gabe Vincent entered the 2018 NBA draft. He went undrafted but was signed to an Exhibit 10 contract by the Sacramento Kings. He played the first two seasons of his pro basketball career in the NBA G League with the Kings’ affiliate team, the Stockton Kings. The Miami Heat signed him to a two-way contract midway through the 2019-20 NBA season. He had his breakout campaign during the 2022-23 season, when the Heat made it all the way to the NBA Finals against the Denver Nuggets . Vincent averaged 9.4 points, 2.1 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game in the regular season. He was even better during their NBA Finals run, putting up 12.7 points, 1.4 rebounds and 3.5 assists in 22 games as the Heat lost to the Nuggets in five. The Los Angeles Lakers signed him that summer to a three-year, $33 million contract. However, his debut season with the Lakers was marred by a knee injury, limiting him to just 11 games. He never got his footing in Los Angeles and was traded to the Atlanta Hawks midway through the final year of his deal. item.title: Vikings trade rumor details deadline plans at quarterback, two potential options
item.description: Nobody was expecting Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz to play at an elite level on Monday night, but I’m not sure anyone expected him to play that bad. Saying Wentz struggled against the Buffalo Bills would be an understatement. The veteran signal-caller had one of the worst performances anyone has ever seen from a quarterback. And, that performance, along with the struggles Kyler Murray has seen this season, leaves the Vikings with a desperate need for a quarterback trade. On that front, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that the Vikings will explore a trade for a quarterback at the deadline, which falls on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET. MORE: Puka Nacua injury update from Rams confirms severity, return timeline “I know the Minnesota Vikings are going to explore their options (at quarterback),” Rapoport said during the Monday Night Football broadcast. Rapoport went on to mention both Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones as potential options. However, Rapoport notes that the Raiders have shown zero interest in wanting to trade Cousins. MORE: Josh Jacobs injury update confirms need for surgery, return timeline “They actually have two pretty good options… Here’s what the Vikings have: they have Kirk Cousins, obviously played for them, played for Kevin O’Connell. The Raiders have shown no indication that they would trade him, but at least they could call and see what is there. “And then they have Daniel Jones, who obviously was in their building a couple of years ago on the practice squad. Playing still for the Colts. A Colts season that has gone the opposite of where they want to go. Those are two pretty solid options who could be had for draft pick compensation that wouldn’t kill the Vikings. I would expect them to at least look into it tomorrow.” Are Kirk Cousins, Daniel Jones available? Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins (8) signals during the second quarter against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi’s Stadium. Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) As Rapoport noted, the Raiders appear to be keen on keeping Cousins and it’s understandable why, as Las Vegas still has a shot at the playoffs. Jones is probably the more realistic option because of the impending fire sale the Colts appear set to embark on. But The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported over the weekend that the Colts informed Jones they will not trade him at the deadline. MORE: Troy Aikman, Joe Buck able to laugh again thanks to Wentz’ performance “The Colts informed QB Daniel Jones on Saturday they’re not trading him by Tuesday’s deadline,” Pelissero wrote. Now, as we’ve seen in recent weeks, just about anyone can be had if a team is willing to overpay. It’s conceivable the Vikings could do just that to land either Cousins or Jones. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: 3 Key Takeaways from Hornets Big Win Over Cavaliers
item.description: Cleveland Cavaliers guard Tyrese Proctor (24) shoots the ball defended by Charlotte Hornets forward Tidjane Salaun (31) during the game at Spectrum Center | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The Charlotte Hornets snapped a six-game losing skid with an emphatic 124-112 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers at Spectrum Center on Monday night. Operating without key rotational pillars Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel, Dennis Schröder , Moussa Diabaté , and Grant Williams , head coach Charles Lee’s starting group generated unexpected answers against a formidable Eastern Conference opponent. Rather than folding under structural strain, Charlotte controlled the game’s rhythm from deep, pushing their lead to as many as 33 points before navigating late-game turbulence. Beyond the surprising final score, three critical post-game takeaways stand out from Charlotte’s performance. Grayson Allen and Naz Reid Deliver Primary Offensive Punch Charlotte Hornets guard Grayson Allen (8) makes a slam dunk against the Cleveland Cavaliers during the game at Spectrum Center. Photo Credit: Jim Dedmon, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect With the Hornets number-one option, Miller, sidelined , Charlotte required high usage from its established veterans. Grayson Allen and Naz Reid stepped into the spotlight and completely anchored the offense. Allen put on an absolute perimeter shooting display, pouring in a team-high 27 points while knocking down 6-of-12 three-pointers. His sharp movement off screens and willingness to pull up in transition kept Cleveland’s defense stretched out and unable to pack the paint. Operating alongside him in the frontcourt, Reid put together a dominant 25-point, 13-rebound double-double. He punished Cleveland out of the high post, knocking down four triples of his own while grabbing 12 defensive boards to secure possessions. Combined, Allen and Reid supplied 52 points, giving Charlotte the exact scoring firepower required to dictate terms. Ryan Kalkbrenner’s Glass Control Changes the Game Charlotte Hornets center Ryan Kalkbrenner (11) back on defense against Cleveland Cavaliers forward Riley Minix (12) during the first half at Spectrum Center. Photo Credit: Jim Dedmon, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect While Allen and Reid provided the headline scoring stats, Ryan Kalkbrenner delivered the most impactful interior performance of the night. Facing a physical Cleveland frontcourt, Kalkbrenner fundamentally altered the game’s physical dynamic through relentless work on the boards. Kalkbrenner snatched a game-high 15 total rebounds, highlighted by a staggering 10 offensive rebounds. His relentless effort on the glass repeatedly extended Charlotte possessions, leading to vital second-chance points that systematically broke Cleveland’s defensive momentum. Photo Credit: Jim Dedmon, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect With the Hornets number-one option, Miller, sidelined , Charlotte required high usage from its established veterans. He punished Cleveland out of the high post, knocking down four triples of his own while grabbing 12 defensive boards to secure possessions. Ryan Kalkbrenner’s Glass Control Changes the Game Charlotte Hornets center Ryan Kalkbrenner (11) back on defense against Cleveland Cavaliers forward Riley Minix (12) during the first half at Spectrum Center. Photo Credit: Jim Dedmon, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect While Allen and Reid provided the headline scoring stats, Ryan Kalkbrenner delivered the most impactful interior performance of the night. Facing a physical Cleveland frontcourt, Kalkbrenner fundamentally altered the game’s physical dynamic through relentless work on the boards. Kalkbrenner snatched a game-high 15 total rebounds, highlighted by a staggering 10 offensive rebounds. His relentless effort on the glass repeatedly extended Charlotte possessions, leading to vital second-chance points that systematically broke Cleveland’s defensive momentum. Anchoring the defense with three blocked shots and finishing as a team-best plus-20 on the night, Kalkbrenner gave Lee elite rim protection and interior muscle that offset Cleveland’s baseline height advantage. Balanced Perimeter Spacing Offsets Backcourt Constraints With Coby White operating on a managed 20-minute workload, Charlotte’s backcourt structure required disciplined execution from secondary contributors. White managed the floor effectively, finishing with 9 assists against just 3 turnovers, while Charlotte’s secondary floor-spacers kept the offense flowing during bench shifts. Tidjane Salaün provided crucial scoring relief during his shift, knocking down three triples en route to 14 points. Meanwhile, Christian Anderson Jr. added 9 points on 3-of-4 shooting from deep off the bench, and Sion James chipped in 11 points. As a collective unit, the Hornets connected on 23-of-46 three-point attempts (50%), weaponizing pristine floor spacing to reverse their recent shooting struggles. Last Word on Hornets Big Win This victory over Cleveland is far more important than just a single home win; it provides a clear operational blueprint for Lee’s system moving forward. Navigating severe injury hits forces young players like Kalkbrenner, Salaün Anderson Jr. and Steinbach into high-leverage roles where developmental growth accelerates out of necessity. While health remains the primary factor for Charlotte’s ultimate ceiling this season, executing a 124-point performance while curbing live-ball turnovers proves that Lee’s culture and tactical principles can win games even under heavy structural strain. item.title: Lakers big Walker Kessler’s take on Collin Sexton team-up will hit Jazz fans in the feels
item.description: Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Lakers big Walker Kessler’s take on Collin Sexton team-up will hit Jazz fans in the feels appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the Los Angeles Lakers being on the second night of a back-to-back, they decided to sit out Austin Reaves — with Luka Doncic coming back from a one-game absence. This left a secondary playmaking void for the Lakers, which Collin Sexton gladly filled. He finished with 18 points and six assists in a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks, and his chemistry with Walker Kessler was also in full display. Sexton and Kessler have pre-existing chemistry dating back to their time together on the Utah Jazz. They played together for three full seasons, so it’s not too surprising that the Lakers are benefitting from the connection these two have. Kessler also had a big game against the Hawks, thanks in part to some dimes he got from Sexton, finishing with 21 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal, and one block. “That goes back a long time ago. I’ve known him for a long time, so we definitely got really good chemistry,” Kessler said after the game, per Benjamin Royer of the Orange County Register. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Lakers would have had a much more difficult time on the night if it weren’t for Sexton . He caused havoc on both ends against the Hawks, and it’s his relentlessness when going downhill that opened up a lot of scoring opportunities for his former Jazz teammate. Kessler on the other hand, continues to be a monster on both ends of the floor — proving to be well worth the $130 million the Lakers committed to him in a sign-and-trade this offseason. He plays absolutely huge, contests nearly every shot, and he provides solidity on the glass as well. The Lakers are now 10-2 on the season, and their offseason dealings have looked like genius moves thus far. item.content:encoded: Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Lakers big Walker Kessler’s take on Collin Sexton team-up will hit Jazz fans in the feels appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the Los Angeles Lakers being on the second night of a back-to-back, they decided to sit out Austin Reaves — with Luka Doncic coming back from a one-game absence. This left a secondary playmaking void for the Lakers, which Collin Sexton gladly filled. He finished with 18 points and six assists in a 124-114 win over the Atlanta Hawks, and his chemistry with Walker Kessler was also in full display. Sexton and Kessler have pre-existing chemistry dating back to their time together on the Utah Jazz. They played together for three full seasons, so it’s not too surprising that the Lakers are benefitting from the connection these two have. Kessler also had a big game against the Hawks, thanks in part to some dimes he got from Sexton, finishing with 21 points, 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal, and one block. “That goes back a long time ago. I’ve known him for a long time, so we definitely got really good chemistry,” Kessler said after the game, per Benjamin Royer of the Orange County Register. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Lakers would have had a much more difficult time on the night if it weren’t for Sexton . He caused havoc on both ends against the Hawks, and it’s his relentlessness when going downhill that opened up a lot of scoring opportunities for his former Jazz teammate. Kessler on the other hand, continues to be a monster on both ends of the floor — proving to be well worth the $130 million the Lakers committed to him in a sign-and-trade this offseason. He plays absolutely huge, contests nearly every shot, and he provides solidity on the glass as well. The Lakers are now 10-2 on the season, and their offseason dealings have looked like genius moves thus far. They have the league’s best offense, with Doncic leading the way and his supporting cast doing its job, and they will look to keep it going on Wednesday against the Milwaukee Bucks. Related: Lakers star Luka Doncic’s 73-point outburst gets eye-opening comment from Quin Snyder Related: Skip Bayless takes not-so-subtle dig at LeBron James while celebrating Lakers’ early success

item.content:encoded: *Yari demands 1.2m votes from Ebonyi; Umahi promises 1.3m *‘If Tinubu isn’t re-elected, ongoing projects’ll stop’ — Uzodimma *APC has built Nigeria for benefit of few — Makinde *PRP accuses APC of suffocating opposition, exploiting religious fault lines By Johnbosco Agbakwuru, Omeiza Ajayi, Ndahi Marama & Luminous Jannamike Vice President Kashim Shettima has said President Bola Tinubu’s massive investments in security, infrastructure, agriculture and human capital development are transforming the South-East economy, promising to address the region’s longstanding development challenges. Shettima, who spoke yesterday at the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential campaign rally in Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, said the Federal Government’s interventions were aimed at improving connectivity, strengthening food security, expanding economic opportunities and restoring security. He said the administration had demonstrated its commitment to Ebonyi through major infrastructure projects, federal appointments and welfare programmes. “This campaign has been a season of triumph. We have triumphed over the falsehoods of our opponents. We have never turned our backs on you. We have answered your support with projects, and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has honoured Ebonyi through distinguished appointments and projects across the state,” he said. According to him, Ebonyi has benefited from the dividends of democracy and deserves to renew the President’s mandate. “You have stood by us. You have assured us that a mandate is a debt of honour, repayable only through service. Yet democracy demands the humility of asking again. We have returned to seek the renewal of your mandate, to serve you, defend you and stand by you,” he added. Listing the Federal Government’s infrastructure projects, Shettima identified the Calabar–Ebonyi–Benue–Kogi–Nasarawa–Abuja Superhighway, part of the administration’s Trans-Saharan highway vision, as a major initiative to strengthen trade between the South-East, North-Central and other regions. Others are the Ndibe Bridge, which will link Ebonyi with Cross River State; the Enugu–Abakaliki–Ogoja Expressway; and the Okposi–Ohaozara–Ukawu–Cross River road. He said the projects would ease the transportation of agricultural produce and manufactured goods, improve market access and reduce business costs. On agriculture, the Vice President described Ebonyi as a major contributor to national food security through rice and cassava production. He listed fertiliser distribution, interest-free FarmerMoni assistance and rural road investments among measures to support farmers. He also disclosed that thousands of Ebonyi residents had benefited from grants under the Presidential Conditional Grant Scheme, while federal employment and digital skills programmes were creating opportunities for youths. On security, Shettima said the administration had intensified efforts to restore stability in the South-East, stressing that economic development depended on the safety of communities, businesses and infrastructure. He cited the establishment and commencement of operations at the Nigerian Army Recruits Training Depot at Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State, as part of the intervention. “The security of the South-East has changed since President Tinubu became Commander-in-Chief over three years ago. We have worked to restore order, and we will keep working,” he said. He also highlighted the establishment of the South-East Development Commission, the launch of South-East Vision 2050 and approval of the South-East Investment Company as initiatives to attract investments and accelerate regional development. Commending Governor Francis Nwifuru, Shettima said improved federal allocations had strengthened states’ capacity to provide infrastructure and essential services. Yari, Umahi demand 1.3m votes Meanwhile, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, challenged Ebonyi APC members to deliver at least 1.2 million votes for Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. Yari, who said he obtained the figures from the Minister of Works, David Umahi, noted that Ebonyi had about 1.8 million registered voters, with 1.5 million PVCs collected. “On behalf of Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, I am setting my target. My target is a minimum of 1.2 million votes,” he declared. Umahi, however, raised the target to 1.3 million votes, assuring the President that Ebonyi would deliver the figure. “We are showing the whole world that Ebonyi State belongs to the APC. We all know there is no NDC or any other party in Ebonyi State,” he said. He credited Tinubu with reviving the 65-kilometre Afikpo–Uturu–Okigwe road project, valued at N193 billion, saying it was already 40 per cent completed. ‘Ongoing projects’ll stop without Tinubu’ Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, warned that ongoing Federal Government projects could be abandoned if Tinubu failed to secure re-election. “Our responsibility will start from now to go and look for our PVC. That is the weapon, because if Bola Tinubu is not re-elected, all these ongoing projects will stop. “There is no name on the ballot paper called President Bola Tinubu. What is on the ballot paper is APC, and I invite all of you to vote for APC,” he said. Director of Mobilisation of the campaign council, Senator Adams Oshiomhole, attacked former Rivers State Governor and ADC vice-presidential candidate, Rotimi Amaechi, describing him as a serial loser. He recalled Amaechi’s court challenge to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s emergence as the presidential candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, alleging irregularities in the nomination process. “If Amaechi accuses his former boss of rigging, are you the ones who will disagree with him?” Oshiomhole asked. Ebonyi Governor, Francis Nwifuru, said the state’s support for Tinubu was based on performance rather than sentiments. “It is rooted in evidence, conviction and gratitude,” he said. He, however, appealed to the President to address the state’s electricity infrastructure deficit, noting that Ebonyi was the only state without a 330kV transmission line. “This has adversely affected our drive to industrialise this great state. Your Excellency, we kindly request that you consider making funds available for us to embark on the project or take over its installation,” he said. Representing the APC National Chairman, the party’s National Vice Chairman, South-East, Ben Nwoye, urged members to vote APC at all levels in the January 16 and February 6 elections. APC has built Nigeria for few — Makinde Meanwhile, presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Seyi Makinde, accused the Tinubu administration of building a Nigeria that works only for the privileged few. Speaking at the party’s presidential campaign rally in Jos, Plateau State, Makinde alleged that the APC had appropriated his party’s policy ideas, particularly its RESET Agenda, while failing to improve Nigerians’ living conditions. “When we unveiled our RESET Agenda, I said in Abuja that they would soon start stealing our ideas. Now they have started. They say theirs is ‘Reform to Prosperity’. They now say they want a Nigeria that will work for everybody. What have they been doing over the past three years? “They have built a Nigeria that works only for them. Send the oppressors packing. Send them back to Lagos, and let us bring in the team that will reset Nigeria,” he said. Makinde identified insecurity as a major obstacle to Plateau’s economic potential, promising that an APM government would prioritise security, tourism and job creation. He said restoring peace would attract tourists, expand the state’s economy and create employment for youths. “Security is a major pillar of the RESET Agenda. Once we start attracting tourists, our economy on the Plateau will expand, and we will create jobs for our teeming youths,” he said. He urged supporters to take the

item.title: Horsepower or Horseplay? Individual performances to highlight from Colts’ Week 9 loss to Cowboys
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 8: Seth McGowan #20 of the Indianapolis Colts celebrates during the fourth quarter of a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts lost to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, 23-27, which wasn’t unexpected by any means given that the season has quickly snowballed into another lost year—with a fire sale now fully underway. To their credit, the reeling Colts, who have now lost 5 straight games and 14 of their last 16 games dating back to last season’s brutal final stretch, showed more fight than in last weekend’s blowout ‘laugher’ loss in Jacksonville. Let’s get to the positives, the negatives, and maybe even a little in between: Horsepower Young Defensive Line: Despite veteran DeForest Buckner having departed back to the Bay, it was impressive to watch some of the ‘young pup’ Colts defensive linemen battle out there, including defensive tackle Ade Adebawore (5 QB pressures) , rookie Caden Curry (a sack and a fumble recovery), Laiatu Latu (a sack), and yes, even 2nd-year pro Jaylahn Tuimoloau (a sack), who’s begun to finally round into form, with longtime nose tackle Grover Stewart remaining the ‘veteran voice.’ RB Seth McGowan: In the midst of Jonathan Taylor trade rumors, McGowan has seen an increased workload as of late and taken advantage, averaging 7.5 yards per carry on 6 carries in this one, including a short 2-yard touchdown run near midway through the first quarter . I still think I’d ideally like McGowan more as a change-of-pace or the 2nd head of a two headed running back attack, than a featured every down rusher, but the rookie 7th round pick has been a pleasant find for Indianapolis so far this season and could be poised for a bigger role if Taylor is indeed moved before Tuesday’s trade deadline. WR Ashton Dulin: The 29-year-old continues to be one of the longer tenured ‘fan favorites’ still remaining on the Colts roster, as he’s gone from undrafted free agent to core special teamer to even starting wideout at times. Dulin showcased his elite speed in this one, turning a short Colts quarterback Daniel Jones wide receiver screen pass into a 55-yard touchdown catch-and-run down the sideline . Rookie Defenders: Safety Hunter Wohler, who missed all of his debut season with a season-ending Lisfranc injury, had a team-high 16 tackles (6 solo) filling in for injured starting rookie safety AJ Haulcy and was a force in run defense. Meanwhile, the pair of Colts rookie linebackers were also active, as CJ Allen had 10 tackles (4 solo) and Bryce Boettcher added 12 tackles (4 solo) respectively. That’ll certainly play. Spencer Shrader: Having his worst game of the season 2 weeks ago in Minnesota, Shrader looked more like himself, converting all 3 of his field goal attempts of 47-yards, 59-yards, and 50-yards . item.content:encoded: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 8: Seth McGowan #20 of the Indianapolis Colts celebrates during the fourth quarter of a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts lost to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, 23-27, which wasn’t unexpected by any means given that the season has quickly snowballed into another lost year—with a fire sale now fully underway. To their credit, the reeling Colts, who have now lost 5 straight games and 14 of their last 16 games dating back to last season’s brutal final stretch, showed more fight than in last weekend’s blowout ‘laugher’ loss in Jacksonville. Let’s get to the positives, the negatives, and maybe even a little in between: Horsepower Young Defensive Line: Despite veteran DeForest Buckner having departed back to the Bay, it was impressive to watch some of the ‘young pup’ Colts defensive linemen battle out there, including defensive tackle Ade Adebawore (5 QB pressures) , rookie Caden Curry (a sack and a fumble recovery), Laiatu Latu (a sack), and yes, even 2nd-year pro Jaylahn Tuimoloau (a sack), who’s begun to finally round into form, with longtime nose tackle Grover Stewart remaining the ‘veteran voice.’ RB Seth McGowan: In the midst of Jonathan Taylor trade rumors, McGowan has seen an increased workload as of late and taken advantage, averaging 7.5 yards per carry on 6 carries in this one, including a short 2-yard touchdown run near midway through the first quarter . I still think I’d ideally like McGowan more as a change-of-pace or the 2nd head of a two headed running back attack, than a featured every down rusher, but the rookie 7th round pick has been a pleasant find for Indianapolis so far this season and could be poised for a bigger role if Taylor is indeed moved before Tuesday’s trade deadline. WR Ashton Dulin: The 29-year-old continues to be one of the longer tenured ‘fan favorites’ still remaining on the Colts roster, as he’s gone from undrafted free agent to core special teamer to even starting wideout at times. Dulin showcased his elite speed in this one, turning a short Colts quarterback Daniel Jones wide receiver screen pass into a 55-yard touchdown catch-and-run down the sideline . Rookie Defenders: Safety Hunter Wohler, who missed all of his debut season with a season-ending Lisfranc injury, had a team-high 16 tackles (6 solo) filling in for injured starting rookie safety AJ Haulcy and was a force in run defense. Meanwhile, the pair of Colts rookie linebackers were also active, as CJ Allen had 10 tackles (4 solo) and Bryce Boettcher added 12 tackles (4 solo) respectively. That’ll certainly play. Spencer Shrader: Having his worst game of the season 2 weeks ago in Minnesota, Shrader looked more like himself, converting all 3 of his field goal attempts of 47-yards, 59-yards, and 50-yards . Perhaps most telling, the Cowboys coaching staff changed their minds on accepting a penalty, which the officiating crew said was legal(?), when they saw Shrader trotting on the field for a potential 61-yard field goal attempt. Horseplay QB Daniel Jones: At one point, the Colts had just 8 total passing yards midway through the 2nd quarter. Look, some of the wideouts playing meaningful snaps are preseason guys, and the offensive line hasn’t been great, especially in light of trading All-Pro left guard Quenton Nelson. However, it’s hard to win when your starting quarterback is dinking and dunking or checking down and rarely challenges the opposing defense downfield. At a certain point, you have to trust your receivers to win their one-on-one matchups downfield. This wasn’t a great Dallas defense coming in either, surrendering the 27th most points (26.6 avg. ppg). Jones’ game-sealing interception facing pass pressure off his back foot was about as predictable as it gets. RB: Jonathan Taylor: The main topic of ongoing national Colts trade rumors hasn’t looked like himself the past two weeks, perhaps making ‘business decisions’ or maybe because with limited carries in back-to-back games, he’s had trouble getting into the flow of the game. I’ve always thought Taylor is someone who gets better during the course of a game with the more carries he gets, sort of like a heavyweight fighter wearing the opponent down round-after-round, before eventually breaking a big ‘TKO’ run late. I’m not going to make excuses for him, because his fumble early in the 4th quarter with the Colts threatening to score a touchdown in the red zone simply can’t happen—and he has to keep his pad level down for that matter. That being said, if Taylor stays past the deadline, I think he’ll look more like his old self. I wouldn’t expect him to get 30 carries in a game anymore this season, but closer to the 20 carry mark we’ve seen. WR Josh Downs: Normally “Mr. Reliable” as a 3rd down slot target, Downs has been “Mr. Drops” over the past two weeks since reportedly requesting a trade from the Colts. He had a 3rd and 8 drop early in the 2nd quarte r , and then followed suit again with 1:45 left in the 4th quarter . If Downs wants to depart, fine, but he hasn’t backed up his surprising request with his play on the field, when such trade requests are typically reserved for more proven players with a longstanding history of production. The Colts are holding out hope for a 3rd round pick to move him, but after his recent performances, they may be realistically still looking at a 4th round pick. In the battle of ‘Downs brothers,’ his younger brother, starting Dallas safety, Caleb Downs, clearly got the upper hand of big brother with the game-clinching interception off Jones, a sack, and even better for him, leaving Indy with the road win. CB Sauce Gardner: Look, Sauce didn’t make the trade for the Colts to acquire him for two first round picks and AD Mitchell, but Indianapolis clearly hasn’t gotten the return for an elite shutdown cornerback that they were envisioning to-date. I actually thought Sauce had played well in this one, until he gave up a back-breaking 46-yard reception to Cowboys wideout Ryan Flournoy with 1:24 left that set up Dallas for the would-be game-winning touchdown. This wasn’t even All-Pro CeeDee Lamb who beat him deep, as an elite wideout that I could actually live with. Gardner’s just given up too many big plays downfield this year.

item.title: Rookie of the Year winners announced, who will get traded & setting the scene for the GM meetings
item.description: Subscribe to Baseball Bar-B-Cast Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube The Rookie of the Year award winners have been announced, with Detroit Tigers infielder Kevin McGonigle winning in the American League and Cincinnati Reds first baseman Sal Stewart winning in the National League, taking home the honors. While both rookies winning wasn’t a complete surprise, there was tight competition in both leagues that had many guessing whether there would be unanimous winners or some split calls. On this episode of the Baseball Bar-B-Cast, Jake Mintz and Jordan Shusterman talk about the award winners, including Jordan discussing his semi-controversial ballot that awarded Cleveland Guardians pitcher Parker Messick one of his two first-place votes and why McGonigle was also deserving of winning the award. They then take a look at the rest of the voting and see if there were any notable vote-getters in what was an extremely strong rookie class. Later in the show, Jake and Jordan each draft five players they think are most likely to be traded this offseason due to the not-as-strong free-agent class we've become accustomed to. They then set the scene live in Las Vegas for the GM meetings, which are set to take place on Tuesday. item.description: How to watch New Zealand vs. India in the 3rd ODI cricket match, including live stream, TV channel, start time in NZ, India, US and UK. Getty India's Axar Patel plays a shot during the 2nd ODI cricket match between New Zealand and India in Wellington on November 7, 2026. Getty WELLINGTON, NEW ZEALAND - ans show their support during game two of the Men's One Day International series between New Zealand and India at Hnry Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Wellington, New Zealand. Getty India can clinch its ODI series against New Zealand on Monday night, when the third game starts at 9 p.m. ET in Hamilton. A win ends the series with two matches to spare, leaving an injury-hit New Zealand needing a victory to stay alive about a year before the 2027 Cricket World Cup. Outside the United States, the match falls on Tuesday. First ball at Seddon Park, a day-night fixture, comes at 3 p.m. NZDT, which works out to 8 p.m. CT, 7 p.m. MT and 6 p.m. PT on Monday for American viewers. Fans in India wake up to a 7:30 a.m. IST on Tuesday start, with the toss around 7 a.m. In the United Kingdom, play begins at 2 a.m. GMT on Tuesday. In India, Sony Sports Network televises the series on Sony Ten 1 and Sony Ten 3, in high definition and standard definition, with Hindi among the language feeds. Streaming runs through the SonyLIV app and website , which requires a subscription. In New Zealand, Sky Sport NZ has the broadcast because the network holds the rights to home internationals . Streaming goes through Sky Go and Sky Sport Now . In the United Kingdom, TNT Sports 1 airs the third ODI , while TNT Sports 2 and 4 also show other matches in the series. Streaming is available through discovery+ or any package including TNT Sports . New Zealand vs. India Preview Getty Fans show their support during game two of the Men’s One Day International series between New Zealand and India at Hnry Stadium on Nov. 7, 2026 in Wellington, New Zealand. India leads the five-match series 2-0 after a five-wicket win in Auckland on Nov. 4 and a four-run victory in Wellington on Nov. 7. Rain interrupted both games, so the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method decided each result. A third loss would hand India the best-of-five series with two matches left to play. More wet weather is in the forecast for Hamilton, and the surface favors seam bowling , according to Cricbuzz . That raises the importance of the toss. New Zealand has won its last 12 completed ODIs at Seddon Park. For the home side, it’s win the match or lose the series. The tour sits roughly a year ahead of the 2027 Cricket World Cup, to be hosted in Africa with matches held across South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia. Moisture, seam movement and rain delays have produced attritional, low-scoring cricket in place of the big totals common in the modern white-ball game, which gives both teams World Cup preparation in difficult conditions. Shubman Gill captains India in this match, with Shreyas Iyer due to take over later in the series as Gill prepares for Test cricket. The pace attack is young (Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar and Arshdeep Singh) and has performed well so far. The batting order leans on Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli at the top, with Iyer and KL Rahul behind them. India is expected to keep its winning combination : Rohit Sharma, Gill (captain), Virat Kohli, Iyer, KL Rahul (wicketkeeper), Naman Dhir, Axar Patel, Kamboj, Nabi, Brar and Arshdeep Singh, in that batting order. Dhir and Patel could swap places, and Mohammed Siraj or Kuldeep Yadav could enter, though the younger pace group has been preferred to date. Injuries dictate New Zealand’s selection. Blair Tickner has been stood down, Matt Henry targets a fourth ODI return and Lockie Ferguson is dealing with a calf issue. That leaves captain Mitchell Santner with this expected batting order, according to Cricinfo : Will Young, Tim Seifert, Henry Nicholls, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Tom Latham (wicketkeeper), Santner, Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Matt Fisher or Kristian Clarke, and Jacob Duffy. Final lineups arrive at the toss. A New Zealand victory would cut the deficit to 2-1 and send the series to a fourth game with everything still open. item.title: Flamingos: Presidency, Obi bicker over access to players at Abuja airport
item.description: *NFF officials stopped me from greeting Flamingos, Obi *Don’t politicise sports, Presidency tells NDC *Keyamo accuses him of hypocrisy By Henry Umoru ABUJA—THE Media Office of the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, alleged yesterday he was stopped by officials of the Nigeria Football Federation, NFF, from greeting the victorious women’s Under-17 World Champions at Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, on arrival of the team from Morocco, venue of the tournament. Read Also: U-17 WWC: How we overcame opening defeat to win title – Oluebube The Presidency in a swift reaction, faulted the NDC presidential candidate’s claim, even as the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, accused him of hypocrisy. But in a statement signed by spokesperson of Peter Obi Media Office, POMO, Idris Zekeri , the office said the former Anambra State governor was at the airport on his way to Enugu and saw the team that had just arrived. It explained that as Obi tried to greet the players, officials of the NFF pleaded with him to save their jobs. The Media Office said in his usual character, Obi respected their position but described the situation on his X handle as a new dimension of toxic politics in Nigeria. Quoting the NDC presidential hopeful, the statement read: ‘’This is the new dimension of toxic politics that Nigeria has developed since 2025. “I arrived at the airport at 7 a.m. this morning (yesterday) to board my flight to Enugu. There, I saw the Nigeria Under-17 girls’ team, which had just arrived and was preparing to board its vehicle into town. “With genuine joy and enthusiasm, I asked my protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether I could greet and welcome the team. I was informed that officials of the Nigerian Football Federation, NFF, had refused and had requested that I should not approach them because, if I did, they would all lose their jobs. “Regrettably, this is not the first time I have been subjected to such treatment. On March 25, 2025, I was in Uyo for the World Cup qualifier. The governor warmly received me and welcomed me at the VIP stand. ‘’Following the match, other government officials went to greet the players, but I was again prevented from doing so. I was told by the officials that they would lose their jobs if I proceeded. “It is deeply troubling to witness the extent of toxic politics into which our nation has descended since 2025. Each year appears to bring further deterioration. This reflects how deeply Nigeria has been affected. “The new Nigeria we aspire to build must have no room for hostility, intimidation or discrimination, regardless of political affiliation. It must be a Nigeria in which unity, mutual respect and our shared humanity take precedence over political differences. A new Nigeria is possible.” Don’t politicise sports, Presidency tells Obi over Flamingos greeting Replying Obi, the Presidency in a statement by the Special Assistant to the Pre

Read Also: U-17 WWC: How we overcame opening defeat to win title – Oluebube The Presidency in a swift reaction, faulted the NDC presidential candidate’s claim, even as the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, accused him of hypocrisy. But in a statement signed by spokesperson of Peter Obi Media Office, POMO, Idris Zekeri , the office said the former Anambra State governor was at the airport on his way to Enugu and saw the team that had just arrived. It explained that as Obi tried to greet the players, officials of the NFF pleaded with him to save their jobs. The Media Office said in his usual character, Obi respected their position but described the situation on his X handle as a new dimension of toxic politics in Nigeria. Quoting the NDC presidential hopeful, the statement read: ‘’This is the new dimension of toxic politics that Nigeria has developed since 2025. “I arrived at the airport at 7 a.m. this morning (yesterday) to board my flight to Enugu. There, I saw the Nigeria Under-17 girls’ team, which had just arrived and was preparing to board its vehicle into town. “With genuine joy and enthusiasm, I asked my protocol officer, Jackie Wayas, to find out whether I could greet and welcome the team. I was informed that officials of the Nigerian Football Federation, NFF, had refused and had requested that I should not approach them because, if I did, they would all lose their jobs. “Regrettably, this is not the first time I have been subjected to such treatment. On March 25, 2025, I was in Uyo for the World Cup qualifier. The governor warmly received me and welcomed me at the VIP stand. ‘’Following the match, other government officials went to greet the players, but I was again prevented from doing so. I was told by the officials that they would lose their jobs if I proceeded. “It is deeply troubling to witness the extent of toxic politics into which our nation has descended since 2025. Each year appears to bring further deterioration. This reflects how deeply Nigeria has been affected. “The new Nigeria we aspire to build must have no room for hostility, intimidation or discrimination, regardless of political affiliation. It must be a Nigeria in which unity, mutual respect and our shared humanity take precedence over political differences. A new Nigeria is possible.” Don’t politicise sports, Presidency tells Obi over Flamingos greeting Replying Obi, the Presidency in a statement by the Special Assistant to the President on Social Media, Dada Olusegun, accused the opposition of attempting to politicise national sports teams and institutions. He said national athletes, including the Flamingos, “represent the entire Federal Republic of Nigeria, not any specific political party or individual ambition.” Olusegun said protocol guidelines for national teams were designed to protect young athletes from “political exploitation, commercial distractions, and unnecessary media circuses while on official duty.” He described Obi’s account as an attempt to turn standard security and administrative procedures into a case of political victimisation. “To spin standard security and administrative protocols into a narrative of political victimisation is a disservice to the unity that sport is meant to foster in our country,” he said. The presidential aide also accused Obi of using “unverified hearsay to build a victim narrative”, urging him to allow athletes focus on representing the country. Similarly, former presidential aide and National Director of Media Monitoring and Rapid Response of the City Boy Movement, Bashir Ahmad, disagreed with Obi’s description of the incident as a new dimension of toxic politics. He said being denied access to greet the team did not automatically amount to political persecution, adding that “protocol, security and administrative considerations must have been involved.’’ He urged the former Anambra State governor to prioritise facts and responsibility and know that Nigeria was bigger than any individual or political party. “A new Nigeria is possible, but not through perpetual political antagonism,” Ahmad said. Keyamo accuses Obi of hypocrisy over Flamingos encounter Also reacting to the development, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, accused Peter Obi of hypocrisy. Keyamo, in a post on his X platform yesterday, questioned why Obi was eager to associate with what he described as a success story of the country and the present administration, despite his frequent criticisms of Nigeria. He suggested that Obi’s intention was merely to seek publicity through photographs with the victorious players. He wrote: “Mr Peter Obi, in all your public vituperations, you often say things akin to the fact that ‘Nigeria is finished’. So, why are you now so anxious to associate with a success story of the country or this government? Just for photo ops? You see the hypocrisy?” Recall that the Flamengos beat Japan 2-1 in the finals of the tournament on Saturday and returned home with the trophy yesterday. With the victory, Nigeria remained the first African country to to win the Under-17 World World at the female level. item.title: Cisco to link all future products to its SaaS-y Cloud Control management tool
item.description: Cisco will no longer create products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control, its SaaS-y management platform that offers netadmins a single tool to manage all of the networking giant’s devices and much of its software portfolio. The networking giant announced Cloud Control in June 2025 and only made it available to customers in the USA. Cisco has previously told The Register that slow rollout reflects the fact that Cisco needs to nail privacy and other regulatory niceties, and deploy infrastructure, before introducing the service to other markets. It appears Cisco is now satisfied it has sorted out those issues. Jeff Schultz, Cisco’s senior vice president for portfolio strategy and marketing, today told the company’s Live conference in Australia that Cloud Control will come online in the European Union, UK, and Down Under in February 2027. Japan, India, and Canada will get their turn in May. Schultz said Cisco is “working tirelessly” to deploy Cloud Control across the world as soon as possible. He also revealed that, starting next year, Cisco will no longer ship products that don’t integrate with Cloud Control. That doesn’t mean those products will be manageable only if they can connect to Cloud Control. Instead, the decision reflects Cisco’s belief that the main thing stopping its customers buying more of its products is the complexity of operating them in concert. Schultz also feels that Cloud Control represents “platform advantage” for Cisco, because when users integrate networking, security, and observability the result is better manageability and resilience. Schultz also told the conference that Cisco will bundle its Thousand Eyes observability and security tool with the “Essentials” and “Advantage” licenses. “We admit it was hard to license and deploy,” he said during his keynote speech, adding that the tool will be deployed automatically with Wi‑Fi 6E and Wi‑Fi 7 hardware. Another product Cisco plans to bring to more customers is Live Protect, a tool that implements compensating controls for flaws that organizations can’t immediately patch. Live Protect currently works on some switches, plus SD-WAN and WLAN controllers. From December, Cisco will extend it to 8000 series routers, secure firewalls, campus gateway, and to Cloud Control itself. From May 2027, Live Protect will work with Cisco’s ASR 9000 series service aggregation routers and Network Convergence System. ®

item.title: INEC and voter register crisis
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has removed 1,608,660 invalid voter registrations from the preliminary voters register and identified 54 staff members across 10 states for disciplinary action, including possible prosecution, over their alleged involvement in registration irregularities. The commission also removed 873 records belonging to verified deceased persons following complaints and objections raised during the display of the preliminary voters register ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed this on Monday in Abuja while briefing journalists on the outcome of the commission’s review of the preliminary register, describing the exercise as part of efforts to strengthen the credibility and integrity of the electoral process. The integrity of the voter register has come under fresh scrutiny following allegations of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated photographs, duplicate registrations and fictitious voter identities in the preliminary register released by INEC ahead of the 2027 general elections. The controversy sparked widespread reactions after images of questionable voter records circulated on social media, prompting calls for an investigation and greater transparency from the commission. Addressing journalists on Monday, Amupitan said the commission had concluded the cleaning exercise covering the 2025/2026 Continuous Voter Registration (CVR), adding that all confirmed invalid registrations identified through biometric screening and public complaints had been removed. According to him, the commission harvested 11,088,238 registration records from the three phases of the CVR exercise, out of which its Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) initially flagged 1,545,052 for further examination. He explained that 1,277,052 registrations were confirmed invalid and excluded before the publication of the preliminary register. The INEC chairman said following the subsequent display of the register between October 9 and 15, the commission received complaints, claims and objections from members of the public, prompting further investigations. He said 268,000 cases were subjected to adjudication, out of which 217,722 were confirmed invalid and removed, while 50,278 were cleared as valid and retained.
